title: Kalaignar Karunanidhi and the Kallakudi Agitation: Defending Tamil Identity on Railway Tracks (1953)
summary: On July 15, 1953, twenty-nine-year-old M. Karunanidhi led the historic Kallakudi agitation, lying across the railway tracks to demand the restoration of indigenous Tamil names over industrial brand names.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 186: நேருவும் இரவுநேரப் பிரசாரமும்: “அழகுத் தூக்கத்தை இழந்தார்கள்”
full_text:
On July 15, 1953, the rural railway station of Kallakudi in Tiruchirappalli district became hallowed ground in the history of linguistic pride.

The central railway authorities had replaced the centuries-old indigenous Tamil name of the village, 'Kallakudi,' with 'Dalmiapuram,' naming the junction after a North Indian industrial cement magnate who had established a factory nearby. To the Dravidian movement, erasing ancient vernacular topography in favor of corporate and linguistic hegemony was an intolerable affront to cultural self-respect.

Under the direction of C. N. Annadurai, twenty-nine-year-old M. Karunanidhi led the direct action campaign.

Marching onto the station platform with brushes and black tar, Karunanidhi obliterated the Hindi and English signs reading 'Dalmiapuram' and neatly repainted the historic name 'KALLAKUDI' in bold Tamil script.

As the horn of an oncoming passenger express train echoed across the tracks and armed police leveled their rifles, Karunanidhi did not flee. Instead, he and four young comrades walked down the platform and lay down horizontally across the steel rails directly in front of the locomotive!

Karunanidhi cried out to his comrades:
"When our language and civic honor are erased, we do not flinch from offering our lives on the railway tracks! The locomotive may crush these mortal bones, but it can never run over the unyielding self-respect of the Tamil people!"

Police opened fire, martyring two protesters, while Karunanidhi was dragged from the tracks and sentenced to six months of rigorous imprisonment. The courageous defiance at Kallakudi forged Karunanidhi’s reputation as an unshakeable champion of self-respect.
